import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# --- Data Preparation ---
# Combine date and time into a single datetime object for easier analysis
df['datetime'] = pd.to_datetime(df['date'] + ' ' + df['time'])

# Extract the hour of the day
df['hour'] = df['datetime'].dt.hour

# Group data by product and hour to find the total sales for each
hourly_sales = df.groupby(['product', 'hour'])['total'].sum().reset_index()

# Find the top 5 best-selling products to keep the visualization clean
top_products = df.groupby('product')['total'].sum().nlargest(5).index
hourly_sales_top5 = hourly_sales[hourly_sales['product'].isin(top_products)]

# --- Visualization ---
# Set the style and create a figure
sns.set_style("whitegrid")
plt.figure(figsize=(14, 8))

# Create the line plot using seaborn
# Using a different style for each product makes the lines distinguishable
ax = sns.lineplot(
    data=hourly_sales_top5,
    x='hour',
    y='total',
    hue='product',
    style='product',
    markers=True,
    dashes=False,
    linewidth=2.5,
    markersize=8
)

# --- Formatting and Labeling ---
# Set the title and axis labels
ax.set_title('Peak Sales Hours for Top 5 Products', fontsize=18, fontweight='bold', pad=20)
ax.set_xlabel('Hour of the Day (24-hour format)', fontsize=12, labelpad=10)
ax.set_ylabel('Total Sales ($)', fontsize=12, labelpad=10)

# Format the y-axis to show dollar values
formatter = mticker.FormatStrFormatter('$%1.0f')
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(formatter)

# Set x-axis ticks to be every hour for clarity
ax.set_xticks(range(0, 24, 1))
ax.set_xlim(-0.5, 23.5)

# Customize the legend
plt.legend(title='Product', loc='upper left', bbox_to_anchor=(1, 1))

# Add a subtle grid
ax.grid(axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.7)
ax.grid(axis='x', linestyle=':', alpha=0.5)

# Improve layout
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 0.85, 1]) # Adjust rect to make space for the legend

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
